subject: SIG: data sovereignty & log handling — prompts, retention, and training
messages_1:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@medtechhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medtechhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: Data handling clarifications (logs, retention, training)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on — we're working through the SIG and have a few specific follow-ups about how Redwood handles customer content related to prompts and model interactions. Can you confirm the following for hosted Redwood API and (briefly) for Dedicated/Private installs: 

1) Prompt and raw request logging: how long are full prompts and associated responses retained in production logs? Do you keep backups or snapshots beyond the primary retention window?
2) Do you ever use customer prompt/response data to further train or fine-tune models? If not, what contractual/technical guarantees prevent that?
3) Are KV cache contents or ephemeral state ever persisted to disk or used outside the serving runtime?
4) What encryption/KMS controls apply to logs and any backups? Can a customer bring their own KMS for Private deployments?

We're trying to map a specific compliance requirement for our regulated pipeline (medical data). If you can either paste short answers or attach the SIG responses and any evidence, that would be ideal.

Best,
Alex
Alex Grant
Senior InfoSec Manager — MedTech Health
security@medtechhealth.com

--
Note: we prefer concise, point-form answers; we will follow up with the SIG matrix items if needed.

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together short, actionable answers below and attached our completed SIG pdf plus supporting artifacts. If you want a 30-min sync to walk the matrix, happy to schedule.

Attached: Redwood_SIG_Response_v1.pdf (completed SIG answers), evidence-kms-rotation-2026.txt (rotation log excerpt), SOC2_summary_2026.pdf (control summary)

Answers (hosted API — default behavior)
1) Prompt and raw request logging:
  - Raw request and response payloads: default retention is 30 days for hosted accounts. We maintain a 30-day retention window for full payloads to support debugging and abuse detection.
  - Short-term debug copies: ephemeral copies used for streaming/debug traces are purged within 7 days unless flagged for active incident investigation.
  - Backups/snapshots: we take encrypted backups for operational continuity; backups containing payload-level logs are retained for 90 days and encrypted at rest. Backups are rotated and pruned according to the 90-day policy.

2) Training on customer data:
  - Redwood does NOT use customer prompt/response data to train or fine-tune our public model endpoints by default. Technical controls: ingestion pathways to our model training pipeline are segmented and require explicit export and opt-in. Contractual controls: standard TOS and data processing addenda (DPA) disallow customer content being used for model training unless the customer signs an explicit opt-in amendment.

3) KV cache and ephemeral state:
  - KV cache is held in-memory on serving instances. We do not persist KV caches to long-term storage for hosted inference. Evicted or expired KV cache entries are not written to durable storage.

4) Encryption and KMS: 
  - In transit: TLS 1.2+ for all traffic.
  - At rest: all customer logs and backups are encrypted with AES-256. For hosted deployments, we use Redwood-managed KMS keys; for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) we support customer-managed KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key). Evidence of key rotation and controls attached (evidence-kms-rotation-2026.txt).

Private/Dedicated notes
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra with committed capacity): retention windows can be customized in the contract, subject to minimal operational constraints; backups remain managed by Redwood unless customer elects a Private deployment.
- Private (customer-controlled VPC or on-prem): customer controls retention and KMS. For Private we ship a configuration profile that disables any host-level collection of prompt payloads by default; you can choose to enable additional logging for support with explicit agreement.

Other controls and mitigations
- Access: only a small, audited set of engineers have the ability to access raw payload logs, and access is gated by role & just-in-time approval.
- Auditability: we can produce audit logs (who accessed what) and a SOC 2 report excerpt is attached.

Next steps
- I've attached the full SIG response PDF (Redwood_SIG_Response_v1.pdf). If you'd like, Mina (cc'd) can walk any technical controls and Rishi can confirm contractual language around training opt-in.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Alex — quick clarifications: 

- Hosted backups: by default, hosted backups are encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS keys. For enterprise customers with a signed Private or Dedicated contract we offer a BYOK path: the customer can provide KMS key material or configure a key in their cloud account that we use to encrypt backups containing customer payloads. We can add a contractual clause that confirms customer-managed keys for backups containing potential PHI.

- Private KMS/HSM guide: I've uploaded a short checklist and integration notes to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/fakeid/SIG-evidence-RED-8421) and attached the KMS rotation excerpt (evidence-kms-rotation-2026.txt). Key points in the checklist: 
  1) Provide a key ARN or HSM endpoint at deployment time.
  2) Confirm key policy allows Redwood service principal to encrypt/decrypt for backup and snapshot operations.
  3) Test rotate and confirm logs in the rotation report.

- Contract language: Rishi (cc) recommends the following short clause to include in the DPA or managed services addendum: 
  "Customer Data will not be used to train or improve Redwood models without Customer's explicit, written opt-in. Redwood will not include Customer Data in training datasets absent a separate agreement."

I'll ask Mina to share any additional technical artifacts you need; we've also included SOC2_summary_2026.pdf in the attachments. If you confirm you'd like BYOK for backups, we can add that to the SOW and surface a sample amendment for signature.

Cheers,

Redwood Inference
